title: Fix the depth
starter:
let depth_in (order : string list) (opens : string list) : int =
  let rec go d best = function
    | [] -> best
    | r :: rest -> go (d + 1) (if List.mem r opens then d else 0) rest
  in
  go 1 0 order
hints: Trace the second example by hand: order `i j k`, opens `i` and `k`. Then trace the first one. What happens to `best` when the walk reaches a loop the value does not use?
A loop the value does not use should change nothing. The answer so far has to survive it.
In the `else`, pass `best` along where the starter passes `0`.

answer.code:
let depth_in (order : string list) (opens : string list) : int =
  let rec go d best = function
    | [] -> best
    | r :: rest -> go (d + 1) (if List.mem r opens then d else best) rest
  in
  go 1 0 order
answer.explain: The loop walks the nest from the outside in and counts the depth as it goes. `best` must keep the deepest loop found so far, so a loop the value does not use leaves `best` alone: `else best`. The starter reset it to 0, which threw away every outer loop.
